summary: TRACK 24.6 mobile tap fix could NOT be verified on preview — a prop-name mismatch in SectionProjectConditions.jsx makes the JobPicker on /daily/submit throw 'onSelect is not a function' on EVERY selection attempt (mobile tap, desktop click, AND keyboard Enter). The touch race-condition fix in JobPicker.jsx is code-correct, but the parent never wires up the onSelect callback, so no selection can commit regardless of pointer type.

ui_bugs.issue: P0 REGRESSION: Parent passes `value={data.project_number}` and `onChange={(job)=>patch(...)}` but JobPicker.jsx declares props `projectName`, `projectNumber`, `onSelect`. Result: onSelect is undefined; every tap/click/Enter throws 'onSelect is not a function' (caught by React) and the popover reopens with the placeholder label unchanged.

integration_issues.flow: JobPicker selection on Daily Report V3 (/daily/submit)
integration_issues.issue: Parent<->child prop contract broken. Also because value= is passed instead of projectNumber=, the `matched` memo never resolves, so `triggerLabel` never leaves the 'Pick a MASCI job — or choose Custom' placeholder even if onSelect were fixed. Both directions of the contract need alignment.

action_items:
URGENT: Align the JobPicker prop contract with its primary consumer. Two options:
  (a) Update /app/frontend/src/components/daily-report-v3/SectionProjectConditions.jsx to pass `projectNumber={data.project_number}` (and optionally `projectName={data.project_name}`) plus `onSelect={(job)=>patch({...})}` instead of `value`/`onChange`.
  (b) OR update JobPicker.jsx to accept `value` + `onChange` aliases (backwards-compatible). Note other consumers (EditProjectDialog, NewIncident, DaySetupSection, AssignmentCreateDrawer) already use `onSelect` — option (a) is safer.
After the prop fix, RE-RUN /app/tests/track_24_6_touch_test.py to confirm the touch-race fix commits selection on tap at 390/430/768 viewports and does not regress desktop click / keyboard Enter.
The TRACK 24.6 onPointerDown fix in JobPicker.jsx (lines 146-152, 188-194) is code-correct and can stay — but it is currently untestable end-to-end because of the broken parent contract.
critical_code_review_comments: JobPicker consumers are inconsistent: EditProjectDialog.jsx and dispatch/AssignmentCreateDrawer.jsx pass onSelect; SectionProjectConditions.jsx passes onChange. This inconsistency is what made the mobile-tap 'bug' undetectable during normal desktop QA — the desktop path was ALSO broken, but the operator likely just did not test click-to-commit on desktop because they were focused on iPhone. The TRACK 24.6 hotfix diagnosis ("iOS Safari + cmdk race") is therefore misattributed to touch when the real defect is a wiring gap.
JobPicker.jsx has no PropTypes / TypeScript contract, which allowed this silent breakage. Consider adding runtime propTypes or a JSDoc @param block.
Recommend a Playwright regression that clicks a job row on desktop AND taps one on mobile for every JobPicker consumer page (/daily/submit, /dispatch, /incidents/new, /admin/jobs).

rca of the issue:
ROOT CAUSE: /app/frontend/src/components/daily-report-v3/SectionProjectConditions.jsx passes `value` and `onChange` to <JobPicker>, but JobPicker.jsx (line 43-49) destructures `projectName`, `projectNumber`, `onSelect`. Because `onSelect` is destructured to `undefined`, both the standard onSelect handler (line 179) AND the new TRACK 24.6 onPointerDown handler (line 188) attempt to call `onSelect(j)` and throw 'onSelect is not a function' — captured by React error boundary / uncaught pageerror. The popover then re-mounts with unchanged parent state and the trigger label stays on the placeholder.

REPRODUCTION: (1) Open https://backup-forensics.preview.emergentagent.com/daily/submit in any viewport. (2) Click/tap the 'Pick a MASCI job — or choose Custom' button. (3) Tap/click any job row. (4) Observe console: 'Uncaught TypeError: onSelect is not a function'. Trigger label unchanged.

MITIGATION: In SectionProjectConditions.jsx replace `value={data.project_number}` with `projectNumber={data.project_number}` (add `projectName={data.project_name}` for completeness) and rename `onChange` to `onSelect`. Alternative: extend JobPicker.jsx to accept both API styles.
